text.p: --BIRTHDAYS--
The first man to see bacteria was Dutch microscopist, ANTONIE VAN LEEUWENHOEK, who was born in 1632.
English artist CHARLES CONDER, who learnt painting in Australia with the Heidelberg landscaping group, was born in 1868.
English actress DAME SYBIL THORNDYKE, who is remembered for her performance as GEORGE BERNARD SHAW's Saint Joan, was born in 1882.
American playwright and lyricist MOSS HART, who wrote comedy hits, was born in 1904.
Italian baritone TITO GOBBI, whose most famous roles were as MOZART's Don Giovanni and Scarpia in PUCCINI's "Tosca", was born in 1915.

Founding member of the Rolling Stones, bass guitarist, BILL WYMAN, was born on this day but there is some dispute over what year. In early biographies his birthdate was given as 24th October 1941. Later it was corrected to 1936 and then a German magazine reporter investigated his birth certificate at London's registry office and found that WYMAN was born in 1926. His solo hits included "(Si Si) Je Suis Un Rock Star" (1981).
--EVENTS--
1537 : The third wife of HENRY VIII, Lady JANE SEYMOUR,
died after giving birth to a son.
1795 : Poland ceased to exist as an independent state
when the Third Partition was negotiated between Russia, Prussia and Austria, dividing the remaining Polish territory between them.
1901 : The world's first "Barrel girl" ANN EDISON TAYLOR
was unhurt after going over Niagara Falls in a padded barrel to help pay the mortgage.
1929 : Share prices collapsed as nearly 13 million shares
changed hands in panic selling on the New York Stock Exchange in what became known as "Black Thursday".
1931 : Chicago gangster AL CAPONE was sentenced to 11
years and fined 80,000 dollars for tax evasion.
1934 : The "poor little rich girl" GLORIA VANDERBILT

custody case heard that her mother had neglected GLORIA since her birth. GLORIA's grandmother gave testimony against her daughter. The ten-year-old had a 2.8 million dollar trust fund. She had been living with her aunt Mrs HARRY P. WHITNEY for many years.
1937 : New Zealand aviator JEAN BATTEN broke the record,
flying from Australia to England in just five days, 18 hours and 18 minutes.
1943 : Penicillin was being widely-used to treat wounded
soldiers. The treatment was being hailed as a powerful new wonder drug.
1944 : In World War Two, the Japanese battleship
"Musashi", one of the largest ever built, was sunk by U.S. planes during the Battle of Leyte Gulf.
1945 : Adopted by the San Francisco Conference in June
1945, the United Nations Charter formally came into force.
1955 : The South African delegate to the United Nations

walked out during a debate on "the racial conflict in South Africa resulting from policies of apartheid." The delegate W.C. du PLESSIS said the UN was intervening in his country's internal affairs and infringing its own charter. South Africa had continually ignored UN calls to abandon apartheid.
1962 : The United States blockade of Cuba began.
1978 : Journalists at New Zealand's "Evening Standard"
stopped work in protest at being called Marxists and Communists in editorials during recent strikes.
1989 : American television evangelist JIMMY BAKKER was
sentenced to 45 years in jail and fined 500,000 dollars for swindling millions from supporters.
1994 : A bus crash on Brisbane's northside claimed the
lives of twelve people. The victims included mostly elderly women on a shopping trip from the Queensland city of Maryborough. A two-year-old child was also among the dead.
1994 : The prosecution in the so-called backpacker
murders trial announced that it intended to call about 200 witnesses in the case againt IVAN MILAT, who faced seven counts of murder.
